display.title: Resolution
display.description: The size the game draws at. The window fits it to the monitor; a 16:9 size fills a 16:9 monitor.

display.title: Window
display.description: How big the game's window is.

choices.label: The game's resolution
choices.note: If the resolution is bigger than the monitor, the window is shrunk to fit, keeping its shape.

display.title: Window frame
display.description: A title bar to drag the window by: switch to another program, then drag it. Needs "Keep playing" behind other windows. Only when the window is smaller than the monitor; the whole-monitor window always stays borderless.

display.title: Behind other windows
display.description: Keep the game running, drawing and playing sound while another program is in front, instead of minimising it.

display.title: Position on the monitor
display.description: Where the window sits when it is smaller than the monitor.

display.title: Stretch to fill
display.description: With the whole-monitor window, stretch the picture to fill it, interface included.

display.title: Wide screens
display.description: Wider than 4:3, the original loses height and books run off the screen. Keep the 4:3 height for books only, or for the whole game, which shows more at the sides.

graphics.title: Enhanced graphics
graphics.description: Draws each frame offscreen and finishes it in a second pass. Lamp light, shadows, the night look and game brightness all need it; Off is the original picture.

graphics.title: Lamp light
graphics.description: Candles, torches and lamps light the world per pixel and stay on their own side of walls; the original lets them shine through walls. The Avatar, furniture and fences cast shadows on the floor and walls, from up to 8 lamps. Only what is on screen casts a shadow.

graphics.title: Sun shadows
graphics.description: The Avatar, buildings and trees cast shadows away from the sun, which follows the time of day; roofs shade the rooms under them. They lengthen toward evening and fade at dusk and in storms.

graphics.title: Moon shadows
graphics.description: At night the brighter moon casts faint shadows, as the sun does by day: strongest at full moon, none at new moon, fading at dusk, dawn and in storms.

graphics.title: Night look
graphics.description: At night the world is greyed, darkened and cooled, so lamps stand out. It follows the game's own light, so it is partly applied at dusk, at dawn and in storms, and not at all in dungeons.

graphics.title: Underwater haze
graphics.description: Under the water, the view fades into a deep blue with distance, red first, and grows darker the deeper you are. The original shows the water as clear as air.

graphics.title: Underwater caustics
graphics.description: Under the water, a moving web of light from the ripples above plays over the seabed and whatever stands on it, softer the deeper it lies. Not in caves and dungeons.

graphics.title: Underwater light shafts
graphics.description: Under the water, sunlight slants down through the surface in beams that follow the sun and fade at dusk, in storms and at night.

graphics.title: Anti-aliasing
graphics.description: Draws the world at twice the width and height and averages it down, so edges, leaves and distant ground stop shimmering, at a large cost in speed.

graphics.title: Draw distance
graphics.description: How far the world is drawn above ground. Further costs drawing time.

graphics.title: Building draw distance
graphics.description: How far buildings and other objects are drawn above ground; the land goes on to the draw distance. Underground the dungeon draw distance covers both. Further costs drawing time.

graphics.title: Dungeon draw distance
graphics.description: How far the world is drawn underground - dungeons, and some open places such as the elemental planes. Further costs drawing time.

graphics.title: Small object distance
graphics.description: How far small things - lantern glows, small props - are drawn before the game drops them. Further costs drawing time.

graphics.title: Model detail distance
graphics.description: How far buildings and other models keep their full detail before the game swaps in a simpler version. Always full detail never swaps. Further costs drawing time. The land has its own setting, Land detail distance.

graphics.title: Land detail distance
graphics.description: How far hills and ground keep their full detail. Past it the game draws them coarse and blurred, and they sharpen as you approach; cracks showing sky can open where the two meet.

graphics.title: Game brightness
graphics.description: Applies the game's own brightness setting to the game's window only. Ignored leaves the picture at full brightness.

graphics.title: Replacement textures
graphics.description: Draws images from the "textures" folder beside U9GL.exe in place of the game's own, at any size. Each file is named for the texture it replaces.

game.title: Windows key
game.description: Whether the Windows key works while the game has focus.

game.title: Screenshot (Ctrl+P)
game.description: What Ctrl+P saves into the game folder. Print Screen is left to Windows; Ctrl+F9 still saves U9GL's own frame dump.

choices.label: The finished picture, as the game's TGA
Both PNGs, before and after, to compare

game.title: Gold limit
game.description: The most gold the Avatar can carry. Past 9,999 the backpack counts in thousands and millions, in the purse's own lettering: 12,345 reads 12K.

game.title: Backpack and bag
game.description: Free placement: items stay where you drop them, may overlap, and the backpack and bags hold far more. If you switch back to the grid, items past 20 (9 in a bag) drop beside the Avatar.

game.title: Usable halberds
game.description: The game has a finished halberd, a staff weapon with its own icon, but leaves every halberd in the world as scenery. On lets you pick them up, carry them and fight with them, with the battleaxe's sounds. Off is the original game.

game.title: WASD movement
game.description: Walk with W, A, S and D as well as the arrow keys, and diagonally with two keys held (W and D, say). The spellbook moves from S to E. Off puts it back. The key map is backed up first.

game.title: Enemies in combat
game.description: In the original, most enemies walk up to you in a fight. With Run they run, weapon drawn. Enemies backing away are unchanged.

game.title: Large address space
game.description: Up to 4 GB of memory instead of 2 GB, for many high-resolution textures. U9GL starts a copy, u9-laa.exe; your u9.exe is never changed.

game.title: Seeing into buildings
game.description: How far from an open building its contents still show. At 700 they can vanish from just outside; 1500 is advised.

game.title: Metrics overlay
game.description: An on-screen panel of frame rate and what the game is drawing: general, objects and textures. Ctrl+F12 cycles them while playing.

fixes.title: Start new actors with clean memory
fixes.description: Prevents the crash when loading a save, and hostile NPCs that never attack.

fixes.title: Saves load past damaged creature data
fixes.description: Prevents the crash when loading a save when a creature's data is already damaged: the game skips the damaged part instead of crashing.

fixes.title: Hostile NPCs keep attacking
fixes.description: Keeps hostile NPCs that never attack from coming back when the game sets up a creature again.

fixes.title: Hostile spellcasters cast
fixes.description: Some hostile spellcasters never cast a spell, depending on what was left in memory when they were made. This sets them up properly, so they cast every time.

fixes.title: Teleporting spellcasters no longer crash
fixes.description: Prevents the crash when a spellcaster teleports.

choices.label: On
choices.note: when it steps in, that teleport is cancelled and the spellcaster stays put

fixes.title: Cutscenes start and skip safely
fixes.description: Prevents the crash when a cutscene starts or is skipped.

fixes.title: Flying no longer crashes
fixes.description: Prevents the crash while flying. When the world streams in and out fast, a missing object is noted in the log and skipped.

fixes.title: End spells whose caster is gone
fixes.description: Prevents the crash when a spell lands after its caster is gone, and the crash when a creature's attack lands after the creature is gone. A spell whose caster has been unloaded - you flew or ran far away - fizzles instead of landing.

fixes.title: Creatures stop at a fallen Avatar
fixes.description: Prevents the crash when a dragon attacks a target it has already lost, and the crash after the Avatar dies, while creatures are still around him. Once a monster has killed you, creatures no longer attack, turn toward or measure the distance to a character the game has already removed.

fixes.title: Rings of Fire are not mistaken for spells
fixes.description: Prevents the crash in the scripted fight between Lord British and Blackthorn. When two Rings of Fire overlap, the game no longer takes a burning ring for a spell and deletes it as one.

fixes.title: Skip models the game cannot read
fixes.description: Prevents the crash loading a model the game cannot read. A handful of models in the game's data are stored in a layout the game cannot read, and asking for one crashes it. With this fix the object is drawn as the game's plain placeholder instead.

fixes.title: See-through flames and effects
fixes.description: Some of the game's flames, sparks, lava bursts and other effects were painted on a purple background meant to be see-through, which the game never cuts out. U9GL cuts it out, so they show without purple boxes around them.

fixes.title: Sounds survive a map change
fixes.description: Prevents the crash on arriving at a new map, in the sound update. When a map change unloads the object a sound belongs to, the game measures the sound from where the object was last placed instead of crashing.

fixes.title: Collision checks at a map's edge
fixes.description: Prevents the crash at the edge of a map, in a collision check. A collision check that finds no real object past the edge of a map is treated as finding nothing, instead of crashing the game.

fixes.title: Shrine cleansings always finish
fixes.description: Prevents the crash while a shrine is being cleansed. If the shrine's own rune or item has been picked up, moved or left on another map, the cleansing brings it back to the altar, or makes a new one.

fixes.title: Lett's book teaches from the backpack
fixes.description: Sir William Lett's book in his tomb teaches the last two-handed move, but the game only lets it when the book is read lying on the ground, and never says whether it worked. With this on it teaches the same way when read from the backpack, and when the book is closed a line says whether you learned it. The lesson still needs Adept dexterity and Journeyman two-handed skill.

fixes.title: Keep rain splashes out of buildings
fixes.description: In rain, splashes could show on the floor inside a building, as in Lord British's throne room. With this on, rain that falls into a room makes no splash.

fixes.title: Clear the storm's haze indoors
fixes.description: In rain the whole scene is fogged, rooms included, so a long room fills with haze. With this on, the fog inside a building is as in clear weather.

fixes.title: No lightning flash in closed rooms
fixes.description: Lightning lights every wall in view. In closed rooms and high halls such as Lord British's throne room that looks wrong, so with this on a strike there stays dark. Houses with windows keep their flashes, and thunder is unchanged.

fixes.title: Fix slow motion after long uptime
fixes.description: Prevents the slow-motion animation after Windows has been on for about 25 days. The game counts time from when Windows started; with Fast Startup a Shut down does not reset it, and past about 25 days animation crawls. This makes the game count from when it starts instead.

fixes.title: Let spellcasters' teleports land
fixes.description: A spellcaster's teleport plays its effects but mostly leaves her where she was, and between spells she walks back up to you. This tests the spot before she casts, moves it to nearby ground that fits, and sets her down on the ground - not in the air, and not up on a roof. She then holds her ground at range and is ready to cast almost as soon as she lands.

fixes.title: Chasing enemies find their way to you
fixes.description: When an enemy chasing you is blocked, the original game sends it on a detour to where you were when the chase began, planned as if trees were not there, so it can walk past you or stay stuck behind a tree. This aims the detour at where you are now and makes it go round what blocked it.

fixes.title: Meshes are unloaded when no longer used
fixes.description: The original game keeps an extra reference on some objects' meshes each time it builds their collision, so those meshes are never unloaded and near Moonglow the count climbs by thousands a second. This drops the extra reference.

fixes.title: Free birds stuck in trees
fixes.description: Birds and vultures that spawn inside a tree cannot fly out, and cry again and again. This notices a flying creature that keeps trying to move and cannot, for more than two and a half seconds, and sets it down at a free spot nearby. Perched and feeding birds are left alone.

fixes.title: Doors open and close properly
fixes.description: Some doors swing past closed, wobble, or end up half open but treated as shut, so the next click opens them further. Triggers beside those doors start a second swing while the first is still moving. This lets a door make one swing at a time, keeps a door that stopped short marked open so the next click closes it, and closes doors already left half open in a save.

fixes.title: Shopkeepers stay off their counters
fixes.description: Shopkeepers reading the book on their counter climb up onto it to reach it, and stay standing there. With this on they read it from the floor, and anyone already up on a table or counter walks back down.
